---
title: "A guard or smearing"
date: 2026-11-12
description: "After Milestone 2b, a question about graphene turns into a comparison of jaxdft's gap guard with the smearing other codes use, and into a first sketch of the next milestone."
---

Milestone 2b was validated: self-consistent LDA silicon with k-point
sampling. Its band filling is fixed, with no smearing, so the SCF carries a
gap guard that rejects any result whose occupied and empty states overlap
across the k-grid. During the milestone the guard had caught two test
settings that sat on nearly gapless problems.

The conversation starts from a side question, whether the code could already
do graphene, and moves through doping by extra electrons to the guard
itself. Mads-Peter points out that other codes have no such guard; they
smear. Claude explains that the guard stands in for smearing rather than
adding a layer other codes lack, and the two settle on aluminium rather than
graphene as the system that would test smearing best. Nothing is decided;
Mads-Peter asks for the discussion to be recorded as a starting point.

What came of it: the entry "Towards the next milestone: smearing, metals,
graphene (open)" in the [engineering log](../engineering/engineering_log.qmd).
